property_summary: The `paused()` function must return true if and only if the contract is paused via `_pause()`, but the mutant always returns true regardless of the actual pause state.

For any state where the contract is paused, calling paused() must return true in the reference, but the buggy version returns false regardless of paused state, breaking the invariant paused() == _paused.
For any admissible input, calling c.paused() must return the same value as the internal _paused state, but the buggy version always returns false, breaking this for paused states.

For any state where the contract is paused, calling paused() must return true in the reference, but the buggy version returns false regardless of paused state, breaking the invariant paused() == _paused.

For any call to pause() followed by a call to unpause(), the paused() state must return false, but the buggy version makes pause() ineffective such that after pause() -> unpause(), paused() will still return false, while the reference would return false only after unpause(). Actually, the bug makes paused() always return false, so the invariant is: after calling pause(), paused() must return true in the reference, but the buggy version will return false.
After calling pause() when the contract is not already paused, c.paused() must return true in the reference, but the buggy version always returns false.
For any pause state, calling paused() must return the contract's actual pause state; the buggy version inverts it, so when Pausable is paused the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

For any paused state, calling paused() must return the contract's actual pause state; the buggy version inverts it, so when the contract is paused, the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

The return value of paused() must equal the internal _paused state; the mutant inverts it, so for any setup where the contract is paused, the correct contract returns true but the buggy one returns false.

For any admissible paused state, calling paused() must return the internal _paused flag; the buggy version always returns the negation, so when the contract is paused the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

After initialization, calling paused() must return the internal _paused state; the buggy version returns the negation, so when the contract is paused the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

After an updateLRTConfig call, the onlyLRTAdmin modifier should check the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00) for access, but the bug changes it to check the MANAGER role, allowing managers but not admins to update the config.

After any call to updateLRTConfig that does not revert, the msg.sender must hold the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00) per the modifier's access control logic; the buggy modifier instead checks the MANAGER role, so a manager who is not an admin can successfully call updateLRTConfig, which the reference would reject.

For any caller, updateLRTConfig must revert unless the caller holds the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00) on lrtConfig; the buggy modifier checks MANAGER role instead, allowing a MANAGER without ADMIN role to succeed.

For any caller, a call to updateLRTConfig must succeed if the caller holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and must fail if the caller does not; the buggy modifier checks MANAGER role instead, allowing MANAGER without DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE to succeed where the reference would revert.

A call to updateLRTConfig must revert for a caller that has the MANAGER role but not the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE; the bug allows such a caller to succeed because it checks MANAGER instead of DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
After any call to updateLRTConfig from an admin, the lrtConfig address must be non-zero in the reference contract; the bug allows setting it to address(0).

After updateLRTConfig is called by the admin, any subsequent call to transferAssetToNodeDelegator for an arbitrary asset must not revert with InvalidInitialization (0x8c379a00...) or similar due to zero address configuration; the bug allows lrtConfig to become zero, causing such a subsequent call to revert.

After an admin updates lrtConfig to a non-zero address, calling getAssetCurrentLimit for a supported asset must not revert due to a zero lrtConfig; the bug permits setting lrtConfig to zero, causing a revert in getAssetCurrentLimit.

After admin A updates lrtConfig to new value B via updateLRTConfig. Once completed, calling lrtConfig() should return B (which may be non-zero). Bug allows B to be address(0), so subsequent lrtConfig() will return B (zero), thus the property 'lrtConfig() still returns the value set by admin call' is violated.

After an admin calls updateLRTConfig with any address, calling lrtConfig() on the reference returns the address that was set (which cannot be zero because the reference requires a non-zero check). The buggy version omits the check, allowing lrtConfig() to return address(0). The property is: after updateLRTConfig(X) by admin, lrtConfig() == X.
After calling updateLRTConfig, the lrtConfig state variable should be updated to the new address; the bug leaves it unchanged.
After a successful call to updateLRTConfig, the returned lrtConfig() address must equal the argument passed; the bug fails to update the internal variable.

After a successful updateLRTConfig call, lrtConfig() must return the new address; the bug leaves the old address, so a view that depends on lrtConfig (e.g., getAssetCurrentLimit for a new asset) continues to use the old config.

For any successful updateLRTConfig call, a subsequent call to updateLRTConfig with a DIFFERENT valid address must be allowed (i.e., the contract MUST have actually updated lrtConfig so the old address is no longer the current config), which the bug breaks because lrtConfig remains unchanged.

After a successful call to updateLRTConfig with a non-admin caller, the function should revert because the caller lacks the required role; the buggy version silently does not revert, changing the failure mode.
Only accounts with the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can successfully change the lrtConfig; the mutant allows anyone to update it.
The reference C only allows accounts with DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE to successfully update lrtConfig (reverting otherwise), while the mutant allows any caller to succeed.

Any address can call updateLRTConfig on the buggy version (it never reverts due to caller permissions), whereas the reference version requires the caller to have DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and reverts otherwise.

After any call to `updateLRTConfig` by a non-admin address, reading `lrtConfig` will return the address unchanged on the reference contract; on the mutant, `lrtConfig` will have been changed to the new address.
For any address not holding the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, calling updateLRTConfig must revert; the mutant allows such calls to succeed and change lrtConfig.
After initialization, maxNodeDelegatorCount must be greater than 0, which the reference satisfies (returns 10) but the mutant violates by setting it to 0.
After calling initialize, the maxNodeDelegatorCount must be strictly greater than 0 (reference is 10, bug sets it to 0 which prevents adding any delegators).
After initialization, maxNodeDelegatorCount must be greater than 0, which the reference satisfies (returns 10) but the mutant violates by setting it to 0.
After any successful initialization, the maximum node delegator count is non-zero, which the reference satisfies (it is 10) and the mutant violates (it is 0).

For any successful initialization, the return value of maxNodeDelegatorCount plus the current length of the nodeDelegatorQueue must be greater than 0, meaning it's possible to add at least one node delegator; the bug sets maxNodeDelegatorCount to 0 making the sum 0 after init, so no delegator can ever be added.
After initialization, maxNodeDelegatorCount must be 10; in the buggy version it remains 0, which changes the addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue limit.

The buggy version's initialize leaves maxNodeDelegatorCount at 0, making addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue always revert with MaximumNodeDelegatorCountReached when any new delegator is added, while the reference correctly sets it to 10 and allows additions up to 10.

After initialize, adding any non-empty array of node delegator contracts via addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue must succeed (not revert with MaximumNodeDelegatorCountReached) provided the resulting queue length does not exceed 10, which the reference satisfies by initializing maxNodeDelegatorCount to 10, but the buggy version defaults it to 0 causing always a revert.

For any allowed initialization and any subsequent call to addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with exactly one address, if the resulting queue length is 1 then the call must succeed; the reference initializes maxNodeDelegatorCount to 10 and therefore allows queue length 1, but the buggy version leaves maxNodeDelegatorCount at 0 and always reverts with MaximumNodeDelegatorCountReached.

After initialization, addNodeDelegatorContractToQueue with a non-empty array must not revert with MaximumNodeDelegatorCountReached as long as the resulting queue length <= 10, which the reference satisfies by setting maxNodeDelegatorCount to 10 but the bug sets it to 0, causing immediate revert.

After initialization, the contract should return true for _getInitializedVersion() > 0 indicating it has been initialized; the buggy version fails to set _initialized, so _getInitializedVersion() remains 0.
After initialization, calling initialize again must revert; the buggy version allows re-initialization.
After a successful `initialize` call by any non-zero admin address, the contract must return `_getInitializedVersion() == 1`; the buggy version fails to set the version and returns 0.

After a successful initialize call, the reentrancy guard status _reentrancyGuardEntered() must be reset to false; the buggy version fails to set _initialized, enabling repeated initialization which leaves the contract in a re-entered state.

After initialize(address) succeeds, the public getter maxNodeDelegatorCount must reflect the value set during initialization (10); the buggy version omits setting _initialized, which allows a subsequent re-initialization that resets maxNodeDelegatorCount to a different value, violating the invariant that initialization state is preserved.

In the reference contract, initialize() always succeeds when called with a non-zero address, whereas in the buggy contract, initialize() always reverts due to the `require(false)` in the initializer modifier, meaning the contract can never be initialized.
After initialization, maxNodeDelegatorCount should be 10; the bug makes initialization revert, so any attempt to read it via a fresh instance reveals it stays at 0.

After a successful call to initialize, the contract's maxNodeDelegatorCount must equal 10; the bug makes initialization always revert, so any external call to the public getter will read the uninitialized default value of 0.

After any external call to c.initialize(address), the transaction must not revert (i.e., initialization succeeds for any input address), but the buggy modifier always reverts, causing every initialization attempt to fail.

For any non-zero address passed to initialize, the call succeeds (does not revert) on the reference contract, whereas the buggy contract always reverts due to the require(false) in the initializer modifier.
